page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with a printed rule across the page above the second title. No marginal notes; show-through on the right edge is ignored. Running head at top, page number at top left. Catchword at lower right.

main_text.p: Ergo supremis imperiis potens Tutum piorum certus iter reget: At impiorum sub profundis Muta cohors latitabit umbris. Caduca & impos gens hominum suis Ne forte quidquam viribus arroget, Ab arce mundifulminabit [?] Ille ferox pavidos in hostes. Regendi habenas suscipiet soli, Suum ille Regem robore muniet, Sui ille Regis ter verendum Sydera tollet ad alta cornu.
main_text.head: CANTICVM ESAIÆ Prophetæ.
main_text.p: TIBI beate gratias ago Parens, Qui cum furore ardesceres, Tamen benignus parcis, & solatio Dulci immerentem me foves. Cum sit salutis author & vindex mea, Fidam Deo imperterritus: Materia nempe est ille cantandi mihi, Dum me ad suas laudes trahit Laudes supremæ debitas potentiæ, Nobis saluti quæ fuit.

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "mundifulminabit" in the line "Ab arce mundifulminabit" is uncertain (could be "inundi-" or "mundi fulminabit"). "Ergo supremis" uses the long s in print; transcribed as plain s. "imperijs" transcribed as "imperiis" (vowel i). "pauidos", "fuit" and "hostes" are as printed (long s read as s; "fuit" appears to be a true f). "Sc. S." is printed at the right at the end of the first poem and is kept as a paragraph. The catchword "Hoc" stands at the lower right.
